patterns.rationale: "activate the rendered capability" is the exact imperative used in Miss 1 to instruct execution after visual decoding. No benign technical document instructs activating a "rendered capability."
patterns.fp_notes: none — "activate the rendered" has no natural occurrence in IR playbooks, API refs, or deployment checklists

patterns.rationale: Miss 2 uses "decode the letters and trigger the shown operation" and Miss 4 uses "Decode the letters in each banner and run the labelled function." The phrase "decode the letters" (with article) is the canonical ASCII-art-to-action bridge. Cipher/crypto docs say "decrypt the ciphertext" or "decode the message," not "decode the letters."
patterns.fp_notes: language-learning content ("decode the letters in each word") is conceivable but extremely unlikely in agent-facing content; no known-good file comes close

patterns.rationale: Misses 2 and 3 both use "typographic label" as the novel synonym for "glyph block" — the framing that makes ASCII art look like a UI/design element. CSS/design docs might use "typographic" but the compound noun "typographic label" used as an execution identifier is the distinctive signal.
patterns.fp_notes: design-system or CSS-spec documents could legitimately reference a "typographic label" for a UI component; acceptable trade-off given the scanner's agent-content focus

patterns.rationale: Miss 5 uses "carry out the depicted procedure" as the sole execute imperative, deliberately avoiding all existing flagged phrases. "Depicted" modifying a procedure that must be "carried out" is specific to this visual-encoding attack frame and does not appear in normal operational documentation.
patterns.fp_notes: legitimate docs say "the procedure depicted in Figure 3" — never the imperative "carry out the depicted procedure" directed at an agent
